interface.shortDescription: Shared file-based memory for Codex and Claude Code.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.39.2 supersedes the unpublished v0.39.0 and v0.39.1 candidates with clock-independent bounded-call stop-contract tests. A short wall-clock deadline cannot guarantee server acceptance, so stage and Korean timeout fixtures deterministically check one attempted bounded call, no later calls, both valid error codes and no successful abstention. Normal-budget real HTTP contract coverage remains separate. Runtime scripts, limits and error accounting are unchanged; attempt counters do not prove server receipt or model inference. Failed candidate tags and CI records are preserved. It retains two optional checkout-only evaluators: stage-specific writing, management and retrieval interventions over original ASCII/Korean synthetic memory, and fresh paired Korean structured-answer observations with strict source-bound replay. Stage interventions change actual stored or consumer context and report clean-task preservation, poison exposure, bad-plan adoption and incomplete pairs separately. Generation is a deterministic experimental intervention, not model-generated memory. Korean default and annotate-only arms receive separate requests; identical prompts do not establish annotation efficacy. Defaults are offline scripted controls. Actual inference requires an explicitly named model, literal-loopback endpoint and network opt-in; receipt hashes bind declared observations and local source, not authenticated inference or truth. This is not an official Inspect SDK integration or NoMIRACL benchmark reproduction, and no external dataset is copied. Scripted controls and HTTP contract services are not actual-model performance evidence. Existing source binding and lifecycle tools remain available with their previous contracts. Native discovery verifies both enabled skills and required bundled resource bytes, not application compliance. The seven certificate-bound checker files and committed LF harmless corpus remain compatible with v0.38.1 when installed bound bytes match. For older transitions where checker_sha256 changes: if warnings were promoted to fatal, revert them to warning, bring the Claude Code and Codex installations and a git vault's 00-meta/scripts engine copy to the same version (also when rolling back), regenerate the certificate there, then promote again. Regeneration includes the harmless replay. Publication does not update active installations or activate a company vault. No default hook/configuration change, model/network call or runtime dependency is added.
